title: Finding C
summary: White keys have letter names. The easiest to find is C, just left of each pair of black keys.

steps.title: Keys have names
steps.body:
Each white key has a **note name**, a letter of the alphabet. The easiest one to find is **C**: the white key just to the left of every group of two black keys.

**Why it matters:** Note names are how musicians talk about notes. "Start on C" or "the song begins on G" only makes sense once you know where each name sits.

steps.title: Every C on the keyboard
steps.body: An 88-key piano has eight Cs. Each one sits just left of a group of two black keys.

items.prompt: Play any C: find a group of two black keys and take the white key just to its left.
Play a C further to the right.
Play a C further to the left.

steps.title: Hunt for Cs
steps.body: Play every C on your keyboard from the bottom to the top. The app names each key you press, so you can check yourself.

items.prompt: Find a C near the bottom of the keyboard.
Find a C near the top of the keyboard.
Find a C without looking at the screen.
